graph.title: 8x8 LED Matrix Row-Column Scanning
notes: Fix for the validator: each breadboard hole takes only one lead, so the six wires that share the power rails now use separate holes on the same rail strip. 5V rail (tp): wire1 at tp.2, wire4 at tp.10, wire6 at tp.16. GND rail (tn): wire2 at tn.3, wire3 at tn.9, wire5 at tn.14. All holes on one rail are one strip, so the nets are unchanged.
Rail hole numbers follow the image roughly: the Arduino 5V and GND wires land at rows 2 and 3, and the pot wires at rows near their pots.
Parts are unchanged from step 2. Labels were already corrected there: the upper pot (pot1) goes to A1 and the lower pot (pot2) goes to A0, as in the image.

Matrix pin mapping follows the manual's table, converted to the catalogue's R1-R8 / C1-C8 names: pin1=R5->13, pin2=R7->12, pin3=C2->11, pin4=C3->10, pin5=R8->A2, pin6=C5->A3, pin7=R6->A4, pin8=R3->A5, pin9=R1->2, pin10=C4->3, pin11=C6->4, pin12=R4->5, pin13=C1->6, pin14=R2->7, pin15=C7->8, pin16=C8->9.
As in the image, the 1k resistors are on the 8 yellow lines (Arduino pins 9 down to 2), which carry a mix of rows and columns. The 8 green lines (pins 13, 12, 11, 10, A2-A5) have no resistor.
Each yellow line is modelled as resistor leg 1 in the Arduino header, leg 2 soldered or twisted to a yellow wire, and that wire's other end on the matrix pin. The joining method is assumed.

Pot leg holes are read from the image and are approximate, but the nets are right: 5V and GND to the outer legs, wiper to A0 / A1. Pot GND and VCC are interchangeable, so the black-wire side is GND and the red-wire side is VCC.
The tutorial shows no USB cable or power supply, so none is added.

graph_initial.title: 8x8 LED Matrix Row-Column Scanning
notes: Parts are the same as step 1; only labels were corrected: in the image the upper pot (pot1, rows 8-10) goes to A1 and the lower pot (pot2, rows 14-16) goes to A0, so the labels on pot1, pot2, wire7 and wire8 were swapped to match.

Matrix pin mapping follows the manual's table, converted to the catalogue's R1-R8 / C1-C8 names: pin1=R5->13, pin2=R7->12, pin3=C2->11, pin4=C3->10, pin5=R8->A2, pin6=C5->A3, pin7=R6->A4, pin8=R3->A5, pin9=R1->2, pin10=C4->3, pin11=C6->4, pin12=R4->5, pin13=C1->6, pin14=R2->7, pin15=C7->8, pin16=C8->9.
As in the image, the 1k resistors are on the 8 yellow lines (Arduino pins 9 down to 2), which carry a mix of rows and columns. The 8 green lines (pins 13, 12, 11, 10, A2-A5) have no resistor.

Each yellow line is modelled as resistor leg 1 in the Arduino header, resistor leg 2 joined (soldered/twisted) to a yellow wire, and that wire's other end on the matrix pin. The exact joining method is assumed.
Breadboard rails: the image shows the right-hand + and - rails. They are mapped to the catalogue's tp.1 (5V) and tn.1 (GND), each rail being a single strip.

Pot leg holes are read from the image (SIG leg on the left bank, GND and 5V legs on the right bank, with their wires in the next column over). These are approximate, but they give the correct nets: 5V and GND to the outer legs, wiper to A0 / A1.
Pot GND and VCC are interchangeable (symmetric), so the black-wire side is GND and the red-wire side is VCC.
The Uno's 5V and GND come from the board's power header; the tutorial shows no USB cable or power supply, so none is added.
